text.p: Bahrain, scene of sporadic unrest over the last two years, has arrested 60 children, most of them below 16 years of age, the opposition Bahrain Freedom Movement said in a statement on Sunday.

In one incident, security forces stormed the house of Hussein Mohammad Ali in Sitra area, beat him up and seized his two sons, Mohammad and Amin -- both less than 10 years old -- the London-based group said.
Government officials in the Gulf Arab island's capital Manama were not available for comment.

The movement also said Bahrain University professor Zahra Isa al-Zeirah was asked by the government to submit her resignation on January 20 "on grounds she expressed some ideas on the political situation in the country".
Her dismissal was part of disciplinary action against civil servants, school teachers and university professors, it added.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from the Sunni-led government.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds have been detained, including children since the unrest began.
